mapped.scope: Loopback HTTP offers and answers accept exactly 49,152 UTF-8 bytes and reject 49,153 bytes for ASCII and multibyte strings. Rejected offers allocate no room; rejected answers preserve the join and waiting room, then a valid answer succeeds. Both bodies stay below the separate HTTP body cap. Synthetic SDP byte fixtures do not prove a native WebRTC handshake or all QR/LAN SDP policy.

Existing real native UDP arrival test rejects authentic 1,201-byte discovery, then accepts exactly 1,200 bytes with a bounded reply. Removing the receive cap in an isolated copy makes that test fail. Finite discovery cases do not establish every advertisement path or physical network resilience.
